Meet Senator Keefer
Dawn Keefer has been a champion of right-sizing government and reining in government regulation during her time in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2017-2024, and since her election to the state Senate in November 2024. As State Representative of the 92nd legislative district in Northern York County, Keefer cut her legislative teeth during her first year in office, developing a non-taxing solution to balance a state budget that included $1.5 billion more in spending than in projected revenues.

York County Veterans Celebration and Breakfast
York County will honor local veterans during its annual Veterans Celebration and Breakfast on Saturday, Nov. 7, in the Mid-Atlantic Industrial Equipment Memorial Hall West at the York County Expo Center, 335 Carlisle Road, York.
Breakfast will be served at 8 a.m., followed by the program at 8:30 a.m. This year’s keynote speaker will be Col. Andrew J. Bogusky, U.S. Air Force.
Veterans, their families and members of the community are encouraged to attend this special morning of recognition and appreciation.
For more information,
visit the York County Department of Veterans Affairs webpage
or call 717-771-9218.
Nominate a Veteran for a $10,000 Heating/Cooling System
Handyside Plumbing, HVAC & Electrical is giving central Pennsylvania residents an opportunity to recognize a veteran in their life through the 2026 Operation Home Comfort giveaway. The York County company is giving away a new American Standard home comfort heating and cooling system valued at $10,000, customized to the veteran’s home and professionally installed at no cost.
If you know a veteran who could benefit from a new heating and cooling system, consider nominating them and sharing their story. The winner will be announced on Nov. 11.
To learn more or submit a nomination, click here
.

I invite area gun owners to join
Rep. George Margetas
for a Concealed Carry Seminar on Saturday, Oct. 17, from 9 a.m. to noon at the West Manchester Farmers and Sportsman’s Association, 4900 Pine Hill Road, Dover.
Attorney Seth Springer will discuss the rights of gun owners and provide information about concealed carry. Northern York County Regional Police Department Detective Jonathan Bailey, a firearms instructor, also will be on hand to share his expertise and answer questions. My staff will be available to provide information about state services and resources.
This seminar will cover your rights as a gun owner, Pennsylvania firearms laws, the concealed carry permit application process and safe concealed carry practices. Registration is required. To reserve your spot, please call Rep. Margetas’ office at 717-767-3947.
Help Provide Baby Essentials to PA Army National Guard Families
The Pennsylvania Army National Guard is asking for community support to help enlisted families prepare for the arrival of a baby. Donations of new baby essentials are being accepted, including wipes, lotion, blankets, socks and mittens, bibs and burp cloths, pacifiers, teethers, board books and thermometers.
For the safety of recipient families, all donated items must be brand new, unused and in their original packaging. Monetary donations are not being accepted.
For more information about the Baby Bundles Program and how to donate, click here.

For veterans facing rising household expenses, putting nutritious food on the table can sometimes be an added challenge.

, a program of the Central Pennsylvania Food Bank, helps eligible veterans and their families access groceries at familiar community locations, including veterans organizations and military facilities.

Important Notice –
My offices will be closed for in-person services on Monday, Oct. 12 in observance of Columbus Day.
Virtual services
will continue to be accessible via my website.
Welcoming Lenny and Four Diamonds to the Capitol
I recently had the privilege of meeting 9-year-old Lennon “Lenny” Therkildsen and welcoming her and her family to the Pennsylvania Capitol.
It was especially meaningful to introduce Lenny from the Senate floor
and recognize the incredible strength she has shown throughout her battle with Hodgkin lymphoma. After five rounds of chemotherapy and 14 rounds of radiation, Lenny has continued to face each day with a positive spirit and a smile.
Today, with the support of her family and
Four Diamonds
, Lenny is back in school, playing sports and enjoying being a kid. Meeting her, hearing about her journey and seeing her smile was a memorable experience. I wish her continued health, happiness and many more adventures ahead.
Honoring York County’s History During America250 Cultural Fair
I recently joined the York County community for the America250 Cultural Fair and bell dedication, celebrating our nation’s 250th anniversary and our county’s important role in our nation’s founding. As the birthplace of the Articles of Confederation, York County has a unique connection to our country’s history.
The family-friendly event featured local organizations, interactive experiences, live demonstrations and heritage displays. I appreciated the opportunity to celebrate York County’s history and the people and traditions that continue to shape our community.
My School Property Tax Plan Includes Stronger Accountability
School property taxes remain the number one issue I hear about from my constituents, particularly seniors and homeowners living on fixed incomes who face higher bills year after year. My
School Property Tax Elimination Act, Senate Bill 962
, is designed to address that burden while also providing a more sustainable approach to funding public education, including addressing funding challenges in lower socioeconomic districts.
The legislation also includes stronger accountability measures for school districts. Each district would be required to balance its budget annually. If a district fails to do so, it would have one year, with the assistance of an appointed adviser, to return to a balanced budget. If the district remains unable to balance its budget after that period, it would be dissolved and merged with another district. This approach is intended to encourage responsible financial management and help prevent districts with declining enrollment from maintaining unnecessary staffing and administrative costs.
I’ll be discussing the proposal at my next School Property Tax Elimination Town Hall on Wednesday, Oct. 14, from 6-8 p.m. at New Castle School of Trades, 4117 Pulaski Road, New Castle. If you have family or friends in the New Castle area who are concerned about rising school property taxes, please share this information with them and encourage them to attend.
Join Us for a Concealed Carry Seminar Oct. 17
I invite area gun owners to join
Rep. George Margetas
for a Concealed Carry Seminar on Saturday, Oct. 17, from 9 a.m. to noon at the West Manchester Farmers and Sportsman’s Association, 4900 Pine Hill Road, Dover.
Attorney Seth Springer will discuss the rights of gun owners and provide information about concealed carry. Northern York County Regional Police Department Detective Jonathan Bailey, a firearms instructor, also will be on hand to share his expertise and answer questions. My staff will be available to provide information about state services and resources.
This seminar will cover your rights as a gun owner, Pennsylvania firearms laws, the concealed carry permit application process and safe concealed carry practices. Registration is required. To reserve your spot, please call Rep. Margetas’ office at 717-767-3947.

Need help with a state government service or have a question about an issue affecting you or your community? My satellite offices will be open throughout October, giving residents another convenient way to connect with my team and access assistance with state-related issues closer to home.

Life Is a Gift: Speaking at the March for Life
More than 6,000 Pennsylvanians gathered at the state Capitol for the largest Pennsylvania March for Life to date, coming together from communities across the commonwealth to stand for the protection of unborn children. Life is a gift, and every life has inherent value and dignity.
I was proud to speak at the rally
and shared a clear message for all Pennsylvanians and elected officials: “Protect the unborn. Support mothers. Reject efforts to expand abortion access at the expense of our most vulnerable, and never forget that the right to life is the foundation of every other right.”
I will continue to be a voice for those who cannot speak for themselves and advocate for policies that recognize the value of every human life.
Shapiro’s Troubling Health Regulations: Thousands of Pennsylvanians Weigh In
Thousands of Pennsylvanians — including ordinary citizens, school officials and many others — spoke out against Gov. Josh Shapiro’s proposed health regulations, and their voices were heard. Following strong public opposition, the Pennsylvania Department of Health withdrew the proposed regulations on Sept. 25. More than 10,000 public comments were submitted opposing the changes.
I added my voice to the effort through an
individual letter to the Independent Regulatory Review Commission
, as well as a
joint letter signed by members of the Senate Republican Caucus
, outlining the reasons these regulations must be stopped. Thank you to everyone who took the time to learn about the proposal, submitted a comment and made your voice heard.
This is a win for Pennsylvanians today and a reminder of what can happen when people pay attention, speak up and refuse to sit on the sidelines. But this is not the last you’ll see of this issue. The administration plans to resubmit a revised proposal, so I’ll be watching closely to see what comes next and will continue standing up for the rights and freedoms of Pennsylvanians.
Learn more about the issue and the proposed regulations on this
State Health Regulations information webpage
.
Goodwill: Turning Donations Into Opportunity
I recently toured Goodwill Keystone’s Store and Donation Center in Lemoyne
to learn more about their work to connect people facing barriers to employment with job training, employment opportunities and pathways to careers. I appreciated the opportunity to see the operation firsthand and learn how their retail and donation programs support that mission.
Goodwill’s impact goes beyond what happens on the store floor. Donations and community support help provide people with the skills and opportunities they need to succeed in the workforce. It was great to see that mission in action right here in our community — and I even found a few treasures along the way!
Preparing the Next Generation of Workers
The right skills can provide more than a job — they can provide an opportunity to build a career and support a family.
Empire Beauty School in York is helping students take that step
. During my recent visit, I learned how the school combines hands-on cosmetology training with support that helps students overcome challenges and prepare for careers. The school also connects students with community resources and encouragement to help them stay on track.
My visit also connected with legislation I introduced, Senate Bill 892
, which would remove unnecessary government barriers for professionals with limited scopes of practice. By reducing these barriers, we can create more opportunities for individuals to enter the workforce, earn an income and put their skills to good use.
I appreciated the opportunity to learn more about how Empire is preparing students to enter the workforce and support our local economy.

Thousands of Pennsylvanians — including ordinary citizens, school officials and many others — spoke out against Gov. Josh Shapiro’s proposed health regulations, and their voices were heard. Following strong public opposition, the Pennsylvania Department of Health withdrew the proposed regulations on Sept. 25. More than 10,000 public comments were submitted opposing the changes.
I added my voice to the effort through an
individual letter to the Independent Regulatory Review Commission
, as well as a
joint letter signed by members of the Senate Republican Caucus
, outlining the reasons these regulations must be stopped. Thank you to everyone who took the time to learn about the proposal, submitted a comment and made your voice heard.
This is a win for Pennsylvanians today and a reminder of what can happen when people pay attention, speak up and refuse to sit on the sidelines. But this is not the last you’ll see of this issue. The administration plans to resubmit a revised proposal, so I’ll be watching closely to see what comes next and will continue standing up for the rights and freedoms of Pennsylvanians.
Learn more about the issue and the proposed regulations on this
State Health Regulations information webpage
.
Goodwill: Turning Donations Into Opportunity
I recently toured Goodwill Keystone’s Store and Donation Center in Lemoyne
to learn more about their work to connect people facing barriers to employment with job training, employment opportunities and pathways to careers. I appreciated the opportunity to see the operation firsthand and learn how their retail and donation programs support that mission.
Goodwill’s impact goes beyond what happens on the store floor. Donations and community support help provide people with the skills and opportunities they need to succeed in the workforce. It was great to see that mission in action right here in our community — and I even found a few treasures along the way!
Preparing the Next Generation of Workers
The right skills can provide more than a job — they can provide an opportunity to build a career and support a family.
Empire Beauty School in York is helping students take that step
. During my recent visit, I learned how the school combines hands-on cosmetology training with support that helps students overcome challenges and prepare for careers. The school also connects students with community resources and encouragement to help them stay on track.
My visit also connected with legislation I introduced, Senate Bill 892
, which would remove unnecessary government barriers for professionals with limited scopes of practice. By reducing these barriers, we can create more opportunities for individuals to enter the workforce, earn an income and put their skills to good use.
I appreciated the opportunity to learn more about how Empire is preparing students to enter the workforce and support our local economy.
Join Us for a Concealed Carry Seminar Oct. 17
I invite area gun owners to join
Rep. George Margetas
for a Concealed Carry Seminar on Saturday, Oct. 17, from 9 a.m. to noon at the West Manchester Farmers and Sportsman’s Association, 4900 Pine Hill Road, Dover.
Attorney Seth Springer will discuss the rights of gun owners and provide information about concealed carry. Northern York County Regional Police Department Detective Jonathan Bailey, a firearms instructor, also will be on hand to share his expertise and answer questions.

9/11: 25 Years Later
This year marks 25 years since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks that claimed nearly 3,000 innocent lives and forever changed our nation. Four commercial airliners were hijacked and used as weapons of terror. Two were flown into the World Trade Center towers in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the fourth crashed in Somerset County after brave passengers fought back against the hijackers.
Twenty-five years later, the shock and grief of that day remain deeply felt. But so does the courage of the first responders, the passengers of Flight 93 and countless others who stepped forward in the face of unimaginable danger. Just as importantly, we remember how Americans came together in the days and weeks that followed, united by a shared sense of purpose and a determination to stand strong.
I recently joined our community at several 9/11 commemorations throughout York and Cumberland counties. At York Suburban High School, participants gathered at the track to climb nearly 2,200 steps in tribute to the 400 first responders who lost their lives that day. Mechanicsburg Borough’s Patriot Day Ceremony at Center Square brought residents together to reflect on the sacrifices of 9/11 and express gratitude to local first responders. In New Cumberland, the Rotary Club of West Shore hosted its Flags for Heroes Dedication Ceremony, recognizing those who exemplify the spirit of “Service Above Self.” My staff joined the Benevolent and Protective Order of Elks, Lodge 213, in York for its Patriot Day Ceremony.
As the years pass and fewer people have firsthand memories of Sept. 11, it becomes even more important that we teach future generations about that day and the sacrifices that followed. We must never allow the memory of 9/11 to fade. We owe it to those we lost, the heroes who answered the call and the generations that came after to remember their courage, honor their sacrifice and preserve the unity that brought our nation together in one of its darkest hours.
Travis Manion 9/11 Heroes Run
The
Travis Manion Foundation
(TMF) is a Pennsylvania-based, non-profit organization that provides programming, including Back to School Character Days, aimed at empowering veterans and families of the fallen to develop character in future generations. The TMF is hosting several upcoming 5Ks throughout the U.S. in honor of 9/11, including these in the commonwealth:
Lehigh Valley
– Sept. 27 at 2 p.m. starting at PHS Stadium.
Doylestown
– Oct. 4 at 2 p.m. starting at War Memorial Field.
Honoring York County’s Fallen
On Sept. 20, the Central Pennsylvania Chapter of the American Gold Star Mothers will gather at the Veterans Memorial Gold Star Healing & Peace Garden in York’s Veterans Memorial Park for a special reading honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice.
Beginning at 10 a.m., the names inscribed on the Names of the Fallen Remembrance Walls will be read aloud. The walls recognize 1,200 York County service members who lost their lives in every American war from World War I through today, including 351 Pennsylvanians who were killed during the Global War on Terror.
Community members are invited to take part in the reading. Volunteers may arrive at any point during the event and participate for as much time as they are able. This year’s remembrance will also feature the unveiling of new Gold Star Garden greeting cards showcasing artwork from Creative York.
Fourth Annual Veterans Stand Down
Crispus Attucks York will host the fourth annual Veterans Stand Down on Wednesday, Sept. 23, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Horticultural Hall at the York Expo Center, 334 Carlisle Ave., York. The one-stop event is designed to support veterans who are homeless, at risk of homelessness or transitioning to civilian life.
Veterans can connect with VA services, medical and dental care, housing and employment assistance, food, clothing, hygiene kits and a free hot lunch. Veterans and military families who need transportation or additional information can contact Barry Freeland at 717-781-0014 or Jomo Beatty at 717-542-0091. Please help spread the word and connect local veterans with the resources they deserve.
